page: Amazon Web Services m7a.48xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by AMD EPYC 9R14 processors utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 192 dedicated physical cores running at 3.7 GHz, with a 1:1 thread-to-core ratio. The instance is equipped with 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. There is no local storage or GPU hardware bundled with this instance type. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline of 50 Gbps.

In benchmark testing, the m7a.48xlarge demonstrates top-tier multi-core CPU performance, ranking in the top 10% for stress-ng multi-core, PassMark CPU, and Geekbench multi-core tests. Its DDR5 memory subsystem delivers top-tier read and write bandwidth, particularly in large-block uncached operations. The processor's support for advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and cryptographic extensions, translates to top-tier performance in PassMark encryption and physics simulations. However, single-core performance is relatively moderate, with Geekbench single-core and single-threaded gzip compression scores falling in the average range.

This instance is highly suited for massive, parallelized workloads such as software compilation, ray tracing, static web serving, and Redis in-memory database operations, all of which achieved top-tier benchmark results. It also performs exceptionally well in LLM inference prompt processing, though text generation speeds are average to weak due to the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration. Given the absence of local NVMe storage, workloads requiring high-speed local disk I/O must rely on network-attached storage, making network bandwidth utilization a key architectural consideration.
description: Amazon Web Services m7a.48xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 192 dedicated physical cores powered by AMD EPYC 9R14 processors at 3.7 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture and the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it includes 768.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. The instance delivers top-tier multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth, scoring in the top 10% on multi-core stress-ng, PassMark, and Geekbench benchmarks. It excels in parallelized tasks like software compilation, ray tracing, and Redis operations, as well as LLM prompt processing. However, single-core performance and LLM text generation speeds are more moderate. With a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps, this instance is highly suited for large-scale distributed applications, in-memory databases, and compute-heavy enterprise workloads that do not require local NVMe storage.
